chief_complaint: Elevated blood pressure (stage 2 hypertension) identified on recent visit

A single blood pressure measurement recorded a systolic pressure of 144 mmHg and diastolic 83 mmHg, classifying him as stage 2 hypertensive. No antihypertensive medication is documented. He reports no chronic illnesses, and his resolved conditions are limited to acute infections and minor injuries. Socially, he is unemployed, has limited social contact, and has a history of stress, all of which may contribute to his blood pressure elevation. No lifestyle data (weight, diet, exercise, substance use) are available.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include viral sinusitis (2020), acute bronchitis (2016), multiple episodes of gingivitis (2016‑2017), foot lacerations (2017), prior part‑time employment (resolved 2017), and a documented episode of stress (resolved 2017). No chronic systemic diseases are recorded.
social_determinants: Unemployed; limited social contact; higher education completed; no documented housing, insurance, or substance‑use information.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: 144/83 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension). Heart rate 63 bpm. No BMI, lipid panel, glucose, or renal function labs available. clinical_impression: A young adult male with isolated stage 2 hypertension and no documented comorbidities, set against a backdrop of unemployment and limited social interaction. Cardiovascular risk is driven primarily by elevated blood pressure; metabolic and renal risks are unknown due to missing laboratory data. Social determinants likely contribute to both blood pressure elevation and potential mental‑health concerns. Early confirmation of hypertension, comprehensive labs, and lifestyle counseling are indicated.
